title: An ancient Chinese thinker argued that a white horse is not a horse
body: Gongsun Long, who flourished around 284–259 BCE, belonged to the School of Names, thinkers fascinated by how words fit the world. In the White Horse Dialogue the argument runs: **‘horse’ names a shape and ‘white’ names a colour**, and what names a colour is not what names a shape, so ‘white horse’ is not ‘horse’. Ask for a horse and a yellow or black one will do; ask for a white horse and it will not. Whether this was serious philosophy or a sophist’s trick is still disputed, but it points at a real ambiguity: does ‘is’ mean ‘is identical to’ or ‘belongs to the class of’?

slides.text: ‘Horse’ is what designates shape. ‘White’ is what designates color. What designates color is not what designates shape. Therefore I say: a white horse is not a horse.

left.label: Membership
left.text: ‘A white horse is a horse’: every white horse belongs to the class of horses. True.

right.label: Identity
right.text: ‘White horse’ is not identical to ‘horse’: the two names pick out different things. Also true.

slides.heading: The delivery test
slides.text: If someone asks for a horse, yellow and black horses may be delivered. If they ask for a white horse, those horses may not. What is asked for differs, says the advocate, so a white horse is not the same as a horse.

slides.heading: Mocked and remembered
slides.text: The Liezi calls his paradoxes ‘perversions of reason and sense’, and two chapters of the Zhuangzi make fun of him. Yet the dialogue is still one of the best-known arguments of the School of Names, even though only six of the fourteen chapters of his book survive.

slides.heading: Only 6 of the 14 chapters of Gongsun Long’s book survive
slides.note: The White Horse Dialogue is one of the six.

slides.question: In the dialogue, if you ask for a horse, which may be delivered?
slides.explanation: That is the advocate’s test: a request for a horse is satisfied by yellow or black horses, a request for a white horse is not, so the two names ask for different things.
